promptSet.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer with a precise character-pose edit.
Asset type: wide 16:9 illustrated background draft for Project Prowl's four-lane deckbuilding lobby.

Input images: Image 1 is the existing courtyard draft to EDIT. Image 2 is Empress Ebb's character identity and rendering reference. Image 3 is Gale Groomer's character identity and rendering reference. Do not modify the separate reference card images.

Primary request: revise Image 1 to correct Empress Ebb's missing hind leg, replace her smile with focused concentration while she cleans her trident, and unify the whole courtyard with the clean hand-inked 2D cartoon artstyle of the supplied cards. Preserve the wide camera, courtyard layout, character sizes and side placements, spacious empty centre, dusk palette, castle arches, steps, water channel, crates, torches and Fire/Gust/Water banners. This is a calm off-duty scene, not a fight.

Empress Ebb stays seated on the low stone steps at the far right, slightly higher than Gale. Preserve her compact silver-blue longhaired feline identity, turquoise eyes, coral-and-pearl crown, pearl collar, navy/teal scalloped armour-surcoat and gold trims. Her head tilts down towards the trident and her eyes watch the exact part she is cleaning. Closed neutral mouth, gently focused brows, NO smile, NO grin, NO exposed teeth; she is absorbed in careful maintenance, not angry or posing at the viewer.
Move her ONE gold-and-teal ceremonial trident from its old leaned-against-wall position into her forepaws, held diagonally across her lap with its three-pronged head near her upper-right side. One forepaw grips the shaft securely just below the head; the other holds a small plain cream cloth against the gold metal below the prongs in a clearly readable polishing action. Exactly two forelegs, both traceable from shoulder through elbow to paw, with natural compact rounded feline grips. No duplicate trident left at the wall, no floating cloth, no extra arms.
Her TWO hind legs must be individually readable and connected to her torso: show two separate short thighs emerging beneath her armour hem, then two lower legs leading down onto the next stone step to TWO visible rounded grey hind paws, one slightly farther back but not hidden. Give the legs distinct contours and a small gap so neither can be mistaken for a cloth fold or tail. She is supported on her haunches and the feet rest naturally on the step. Keep her abdomen covered. Her ONE fluffy tail emerges behind her hip and curves behind her toward the OUTER RIGHT wall, visibly separate from both hind legs and paws. Do not count a fluffy curl as a leg. No human anatomy, long human thighs, human hands, or disembodied feet. Exactly one head, one torso, two forelegs, two hind legs, one tail.

Gale Groomer remains relaxed on the wooden seat at the far left, wearing the same green/gold captain's coat, green scarf, brass goggles and blue belt clasp. Preserve his friendly relaxed expression, identity and casual seated pose. No new character or equipment.

Artstyle unification is essential: simplify the ENVIRONMENT to the cards' production-cartoon language instead of making the cats painterly. Use bold slightly varied warm-black contours, thinner purposeful interior lines, completely flat matte base colours and one hard-edged cel-shadow shape per major form. Stone arches, paving, wood, foliage and water should be broad clean graphic shapes, with far fewer small block lines and NO mottled surface texture. Cloud banks become a few broad outlined colour shapes, distant castle and mountains simple silhouettes, water simple blue shapes with sparse flat amber reflection marks. Keep the same dusk blue/violet and warm amber mood, using restrained flat cool shadow shapes and small warm torch-facing colour accents on BOTH characters and scenery. Foreground line weight is consistent between cats and nearby architecture; distant shapes are quieter. No glossy dimensional rendering, soft airbrush, realistic material grain, painterly masonry, tiny foliage stippling or isolated sticker-like characters. Do not oversimplify into crude toddler drawing: retain confident appealing linework, coherent perspective, elegant shapes and the recognisable courtyard.

Keep all three elemental banner families in their current positions: brick-red Fire flame, green Gust wind spiral, blue Water droplet. No new characters, crowd silhouettes, text, logos, watermark, UI panels, buttons or card frames. Retain the opaque full-bleed landscape composition with a calm, unobstructed central area.
